introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2023. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators are allowed. Formulae booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) Given that $(x-1)$ is a factor of $f(x)$, where $f(x)=x^3-2x^2-kx+6$, find the value of $k$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since $(x-1)$ is a factor of $f(x)$, the **factor theorem** gives $f(1)=0$.

$$f(1)=1^3-2(1)^2-k(1)+6=1-2-k+6=5-k.$$

Setting $5-k=0$ gives $k=5$.

**$k=5$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) With this value of $k$, factorise $f(x)$ completely. *[2 marks]*
(ii)(a) Given that $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $2x^2-x-1=0$, find the values of $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha\beta$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $ax^2+bx+c=0$ the sum of the roots is $-\dfrac{b}{a}$ and the product is $\dfrac{c}{a}$. Here $a=2$, $b=-1$, $c=-1$:

$$\alpha+\beta=-\frac{-1}{2}=\frac12,\qquad \alpha\beta=\frac{-1}{2}=-\frac12.$$

**$\alpha+\beta=\dfrac12$ and $\alpha\beta=-\dfrac12$.**
themes: sum and product of roots (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) Hence, find a quadratic equation with integral coefficient whose roots are $\alpha^2$ and $\beta^2$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the sum and product of the new roots $\alpha^2$ and $\beta^2$.

**Sum:** $\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta=\left(\dfrac12\right)^2-2\left(-\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac14+1=\dfrac54.$

**Product:** $\alpha^2\beta^2=(\alpha\beta)^2=\left(-\dfrac12\right)^2=\dfrac14.$

The equation is $x^2-(\text{sum})\,x+(\text{product})=0$:

$$x^2-\frac54x+\frac14=0.$$

Multiply by 4 to obtain integral coefficients:

$$4x^2-5x+1=0.$$

Check: the roots of $2x^2-x-1=0$ are $1$ and $-\dfrac12$, so the squares are $1$ and $\dfrac14$, and $4x^2-5x+1=(4x-1)(x-1)$ has roots $\dfrac14$ and $1$.

**$4x^2-5x+1=0$.**
themes: sum and product of roots (additional maths)
